title: Auckland 1918 (catalogue 757): Consul-General Winslow and the US Navy on unknown wireless signals; Vigenère keyed FEBRUARY

steps.what: Both cables transcribed from images 0113-0114, checked on full-resolution crops.
Reply only: repeats at distances 104, 56, 32 (gcd 8); IC 0.062 at period 8.
Per-column frequency fit on the reply: Vigenère key FEBRUARY; frozen.
Frozen key on the held-out outgoing cable: 94/94 letters of English; 0 of 1,000 shuffled controls reach its score.
Eight garbles in the reply located and restored, each forced by its word (mostly Morse confusions, two overstrikes).

validation.notes: A Vigenère key (the 8-letter word FEBRUARY) found from the reply and confirmed on a second, unused cable that decrypts to 94 of 94 letters of English with 0 of 1,000 shuffles reaching its score; the n-gram validator is built for homophonic and nomenclator keys.

outcome.method_basis: Period from repeats, key from frequencies on the reply; confirmed on the other cable.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cable 1: 94/94 letters. Cable 2: 297/305 letters direct, 8 restored garbles; every word read; final OK and 17527 not interpreted.

credits.note: key found and checked on the held-out cable; both cables read, garbles listed, English translation

texts.label: Winslow to Naval Commander San Francisco, 18 Feb 1918
texts.summary: Are automatic wireless stations working between San Francisco and Honolulu on 2,000-metre wavelengths?

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 31 Oct 2026: one complete telegraphic question in English; 9 letters restored over the whole reading.md (both cables), no hole.

texts.label: Washington to Consul-General Auckland, 28 Feb 1918
texts.summary: No automatic stations between Honolulu and San Francisco; wavelengths 4,000 m or above; a suspicious automatic station heard in the US since 15 February.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 31 Oct 2026: four complete telegraphic sentences (stations, wavelengths, the suspicious station heard since 15 Feb); restored letters only, no hole. The 44% sentence score comes from the telegraphic style and PERIOD markers.
